title: Non-Negative AdderNet: Algorithm-Hardware Co-design for Lightweight Defense of Adversarial Bit-Flip Attacks
problem: Neural networks are vulnerable to bit-flip attacks that corrupt computation. Traditional defense mechanisms add significant overhead, limiting deployment on resource-constrained devices.
motivation: Lightweight hardware defense against bit-flip attacks enables secure neural network deployment on edge devices without sacrificing performance.
method: Non-Negative AdderNet with hardware defense architecture using non-positive weight encoding and integrated decoder. Algorithm-hardware co-design minimizes overhead. Defends against adversarial bit-flip attacks with reduced complexity.
key_novelty: Hardware-friendly non-negative adder networks with integrated bit-flip defense via non-positive weight encoding.
limitations: Performance metrics, defense effectiveness against various attack types, and comparison with other defense mechanisms not detailed.
